#### What this PR does / why we need it:
After this PR, libcontainer's cgroup manager is used in order to update pod resources instead of writing directly to cgroupfs.

Further to solving #113857 by avoiding pod updates to be overridden when systemd daemon reloads, it simplifies the code and delegates the heavy lifting to libcontainer's cgroup manager.

@tallclair Thanks a lot for your review!
And sorry for the delay, I was out of office for a while.

You’ve raised two great points in your review that I’d like to discuss.

Firstly, there are slight differences between runc and our current code. While these changes are minor, they could potentially alter behavior. I believe leveraging a well-known third-party library like runc to handle the cgroup logic offers significant advantages. Moving forward, we have two options: either reimplement the same logic with these small changes, or use runc for most operations while writing our own code for the rest. What do you think is the best path forward?

Secondly, regarding testing these changes, unit tests won’t be very effective since we need to test in an environment with systemd running. Are our lanes using systemd? If so, this code would be thoroughly tested as nearly every test goes through this code path. In that case, is it sufficient to rely on the current test suite, or should I add an e2e test?

Thanks a lot!

Can you be more specific about how you're proposing using runc? I assume you mean using the runc libcontainer library as opposed to calling the runc binary? Are you proposing calling into the library at a higher level of abstraction?

> Can you be more specific about how you're proposing using runc?

Hey @tallclair! Thanks for your response!
Yes, let me try to elaborate.

> I assume you mean using the runc libcontainer library as opposed to calling the runc binary?

Yes, I do want to use the runc libcontainer library. The library handles updating cgroup's resources agnostically to whether systemd or cgroupfs are used as a cgroup driver. So we catch two birds with the same stone - covering the systemd cgroup driver case and eliminating the code to handle the cgroupfs case by delegating this to runc.

> Are you proposing calling into the library at a higher level of abstraction?

I'm not entirely sure what you mean by that. Can you please elaborate?

OK, I finally had time to follow up on this. Thanks for your patience!

Yes, I think your proposal to switch to using libcontainer is a good one. IIUC, we already use libcontainer for the initial configuration ([source]), so it makes sense that we should call the same library to update the configuration.

[source]: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2049360379bcc5d6467769cef112e6e492d3d2f0/pkg/kubelet/cm/cgroup_manager_linux.go#L369-L399

/assign @ndixita

Dixi is working on pod-level resources, and has some familiarity with this code too.

Can we just update the calling code to use the [`CgroupManager.Update`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2049360379bcc5d6467769cef112e6e492d3d2f0/pkg/kubelet/cm/cgroup_manager_linux.go#L354-L367) function directly instead?

/test pull-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd
/test pull-kubernetes-unit
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-inplace-pod-resize-containerd-main-v2

> Can we just update the calling code to use the [`CgroupManager.Update`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2049360379bcc5d6467769cef112e6e492d3d2f0/pkg/kubelet/cm/cgroup_manager_linux.go#L354-L367) function directly instead?

Nice catch!
Done :)

As I tried this fix locally, the CPU quota of a pod cgroup was updated to `max` when the CPU limits are resized.

It looks that libcontainer updates `cpu.max` if either `CpuQuota` or `CpuPeriod` is set to `Resources`:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1bbe775d5ffb131636193fe0bc15a8fcc0cd6fd6/vendor/github.com/opencontainers/runc/libcontainer/cgroups/fs2/cpu.go#L29

So, we should set `CPUPeriod` to `podCpuResources` only when `CPUQuota` in a pod cgroup is updated:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1bbe775d5ffb131636193fe0bc15a8fcc0cd6fd6/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go#L677-L684
Otherwise, `CPUQuota` will be updated to `max` when `CPUShares` is updated at resizing a pod cgroup.

issue_context.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Handle systemd cgroup driver by using libcontainer for updating pod cgroup values
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

In-place pod resize with cgroupv2 (where systemd cgroup driver is default) should use libcontainer functions to update pod cgroup settings. Please see this issue for details:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102884#discussion_r1019704157


### Why is this needed?

Without this fix, reloading systemd daemons will cause the change to revert.

I think we need to preserve this conversion. I think this can just be done in the common path, so both CPU shares & CPU weight are set, and libcontainer just uses the correct one depending on if it's cgroups v1 or v2

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1bbe775d5ffb131636193fe0bc15a8fcc0cd6fd6/vendor/github.com/opencontainers/runc/libcontainer/cgroups/fs2/cpu.go#L22

Hey @tallclair!
I believe this conversion already takes place in the current state of this PR.

The `setCgroupCPUConfig` is now unified here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124216/files#diff-2f332b11d91d53583a6eeca75fc6e124aee6bc547a264e6987b89b1c786e0674R257.

In turn, the `Update()` function uses `libctCgroupConfig()` to convert the cgroup config to a runc struct:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b845137026be136ec12d798a2b729ce8b99b85af/pkg/kubelet/cm/cgroup_manager_linux.go#L358-L364

And indeed this function handles the conversion between cpu shares to cpu weight:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b845137026be136ec12d798a2b729ce8b99b85af/pkg/kubelet/cm/cgroup_manager_linux.go#L199-L204
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b845137026be136ec12d798a2b729ce8b99b85af/pkg/kubelet/cm/cgroup_manager_linux.go#L274-L291
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b845137026be136ec12d798a2b729ce8b99b85af/pkg/kubelet/cm/cgroup_manager_linux.go#L259-L267

WDYT?
